actions.reason: b58decode_int no longer does a dict lookup for every input character. A cached helper builds two things for each (alphabet, autofix) pair: the bytes of valid characters and a 256-entry bytes.translate table that maps each character to its digit value. Invalid input is found with v.translate(None, valid). The first character left over is the first invalid character, so the ValueError message is the same as before. The digit values come from one translate call, and the existing 5-digit chunked multiply-add then runs on plain ints. If an alphabet has a digit value above 255, which is only possible with more than 256 entries, the old per-character map lookup is still used. Equivalence output is identical and all tests pass. decode_ir ratio 0.9617, check_ir 0.9952, encode_ir 1.0038 (encode path unchanged).
